speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic; I understand you have a pruritic rash, low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help me determine the cause of these symptoms, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if anyone around you is currently sick?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

The clinical picture of a 11-year-old girl presenting with a "slapped cheek" facial rash (sparing the perioral area) appearing 4 days after an initial viral prodrome of fever, rhinorrhea, and headache, followed by a lacy or pruritic rash on the trunk and extremities, is classic for this condition. No further testing is required as the presentation is pathognomonic.
